pois.name: Roppongi Hills
pois.description: Revolutionary mixed-use complex (2003) by Mori Building — 54-storey Mori Tower, 200+ shops, 21 restaurants, cinemas, and the Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor. The 45m Mori Garden preserves a historic mansion garden at the heart of Tokyo's most ambitious urban development.

pois.name: Mori Art Museum
pois.description: Tokyo's premier contemporary art museum on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower. No permanent collection — only boundary-pushing temporary exhibitions. The adjacent Tokyo City View observation deck wraps the same floor with a 360° panorama at 238 m.

pois.name: Tokyo City View
pois.description: The open-air 'Sky Deck' observation platform at the top of Mori Tower (270 m) — Tokyo's highest outdoor viewing point. 360° panorama stretching to Mt Fuji, Tokyo Bay, and Skytree. The glass-walled indoor City View on floor 52 wraps the same building.

pois.name: Roppongi Station
pois.description: The crossroads of two Tokyo Metro lines (Hibiya and Oedo) and the gateway to the district. The station's giant spider sculpture ('Maman' by Louise Bourgeois, on permanent loan from Mori Building) greets visitors at the Roppongi Hills exit.

pois.name: Roppongi Nightlife Zone
pois.description: Tokyo's most international entertainment district — bars, clubs, restaurants and live venues around the Roppongi Crossing intersection. The area has reinvented itself since 2003: Art Triangle Roppongi (Mori, National Art Center, Suntory Museum) now rivals the nightlife scene in cultural weight.
